text:
maria: Heads up - noticing a sudden throughput regression for low-latency routes in eu-west-1. Rack-5 node gpu-5b shows sustained p95 token latency +30% and intermittent Xid 13s; ECC corrected counts jumping. Anyone on call?
ops-bot: Automated alert: GPU thermal exceeded threshold on gpu-5b (temp=92C). Fan PWM reports unstable; power limit=250W, auto-throttle engaged. Alert ID: alert-78341.
lee: On it. Pulling DCGM and nvidia-smi logs now.
maria: Can we drain that host from the inference pool? It's skewing p95 for the real-time tenant.
jordan: +1 to drain. If we can evacuate pods to other dedicated nodes, do it before we lose more capacity.
samir: I can coordinate hardware swap but need confirmation before draining 4 active low-latency pods. Alternatives: try soft-reset first to avoid immediate RMA. Also saw a config push to rack power profiles earlier today — could be related.
lee: Quick capture from the node: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC | grep -A2 'Single bit'
Single bit ECC errors : 128

# dmesg | tail -n 10
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 13, PID=2439, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12345.679012] kernel: GPU 0000:03:00.0: Reset failed: Device or resource busy
```
ops-bot: Evacuation started: 3 inference pods moved off gpu-5b to gpu-7a and gpu-9c.
maria: After moving, telemetry shows fans cycling 0 -> 70% every ~18s, tach signal is noisy. Could be fan electronics or fan connector. Not just thermal load.
jordan: If the fan PWM is oscillating, power-cycling the whole host could lock the BMC (we saw that last month). Recommend keep node powered but tagged and drained, then schedule a hot-swap of the blower assembly.
lee: I attempted a soft GPU reset: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 1` — kernel returned Xid 13 again, card didn't come back cleanly. NVML still reports device as attached but unresponsive to CUDA clients.
samir: Opening RMA with vendor now. SR#78341 created, referencing Xid 13 + tach oscillation and ECC spike. Vendor ETA: next-business-day replacement for that card.
maria: For routing: can we temporarily shift critical low-latency customers to dedicated nodes in eu-west-1? We need an ops runbook entry on this pattern.
lee: Did that — updated routing policy to prefer dedicated-pool-2 for key routes; it took ~90s to drain and warm other hosts.
jordan: Action items: 1) Add alert for rapid fan PWM oscillation (delta >50% within 30s) correlated with ECC spike rate. 2) Audit any power-profile pushes to rack-5 — there was a push at 03:12 UTC (change-id dc-power-2025-07-14). 3) Add a pre-emptive evacuation runbook for Xid 13 bursts.
maria: Also flag for finance — emergency replacement outside of scheduled capex will hit this month's OPEX. Samir, pls include cost estimate in the RMA ticket.
ops-bot: Node tags updated: gpu-5b -> to-rma, maintenance-window scheduled 2025-08-02T01:00Z. RMA SR#78341 updated with vendor notes.
lee: Follow-up: we've quarantined the node and are routing traffic away. Will attach fuller logs and a short post-incident blameless note once RMA confirmed.
jordan: Thanks all — good triage. Postmortem to include: correlate firmware/power-profile pushes with sensor instability, add automated reroute for noisy tach readings, and consider keeping a small hot-spare pool in region for these events.
